lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the correlation coefficient, slope and intercept in context, and correlation versus causation
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: the correlation coefficient, slope and intercept in context, and correlation versus causation

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: Find the mean and median of 4, 8, 6, 10, 2.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 238 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 21 yes, 27 no; row 2: 16 yes, 17 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 2x + 25, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: The predicted value is 2 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 2 test points.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 2 test points.
Each additional test points is associated with 2 more hour studieds.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set records 7, 6, 9, 7, 17. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 9, median 7
mean 9.2, median 7
mean 7, median 9.2
mean 9.2, median 9

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 207 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 56 yes, 60 no; row 2: 13 yes, 7 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 18x + 35, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional kilometre travelled causes an increase of exactly 18 litres of fuel.
Each additional litres of fuel is associated with 18 more kilometre travelleds.
The predicted value is 18 litres of fuel when x is 0.
Each additional kilometre travelled is associated with an increase of about 18 litres of fuel.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

items.prompt: A data set records 18, 18, 2, 39, 5, 16, 8. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 16, median 15.14
mean 15.14, median 16
mean 15, median 16
mean 15.14, median 15
